label: Early-sequence bigram detector: step-1 input from {o,n,a,l,i,f,p,m} after first token from {i,a,x,f,n,d,m,r,s}, or o as first token
explanation: Fires only in the original phase at steps 0-2 and never at the delimiter or during the copy phase. About 79% of activation mass is at t=1, about 12% at t=0 and about 8% at t=2. At t=1 it fires when the second input is one of o,n,a,l,i,f,p,m and the first input is one of i,a,x,f,n,d,m (plus r,s, which give weaker activations). At t=0 it fires only when the first token is o, at about 0.17 of max. The strongest activations (1.0 of max) are on o at t=1 after i ("i o"), and o is the dominant input token (31% of mass). The weaker t=2 activations (for example x i [o], f x [n]) are left out because they are inconsistent: adding t=2 o lowered F1. It does not fire on b, and only rarely on d, s or r as the current input. It does not fire on first tokens such as c, w, t, y, j or g, and is silent from t>=3 onward.

issues: The explanation says adding a t=2 clause lowered F1. That is false. Adding ((t==2) & in_tok in {o,n,a,l,i,f,p,m} & prev_tok in {i,a,x,f,n,d,m} & prev2_tok in {i,a,x,f,n,d,m}) raises dev F1 from 0.861 to 0.890 and test F1 from 0.859 to 0.888. Mass recall rises from 0.885 to 0.955.

The t=2 activity is not inconsistent. It follows the same rule as t=1, pushed one position later: the current input is from the second-token set and both earlier inputs are from the first-token set (P=0.70 on its own). The label and predicate leave out about 8% of activation mass and about 10% of active steps that this rule covers.

The other claims check out. Activity at t=0 is exactly first token o (precision 1.0, all t=0 activity). Nothing fires at the delimiter, in the copy phase, or at t>=3. First tokens c, w, t, y, j, g, b, e, h, k, p, q, u, z and the digits give zero activity. Current inputs b, c and e give zero, and d, s and r are rare. First tokens i, a, x, f and n give precision 1.0 at t=1, while r and s are weaker (P about 0.64).
skeptic.revised_label: Fires only in the first three original positions. The current input is from {o,n,a,l,i,f,p,m} and every earlier input is from {i,a,x,f,n,d,m} (r and s also count at t=1). At t=0 it fires on first token o alone. Strongest on o right after i.
